title: ATF declares ‘major incident’ as ransomware gang claims hack on investigation system
summary: The U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) declared a 'major incident' after a ransomware gang, Qilin, claimed responsibility for a cyberattack on a stand-alone system containing sensitive investigation data. The attack, classified as a 'major incident' under federal law, requires formal notification to Congress. Qilin, known for its ransomware-as-a-service operations, has not provided evidence of the breach, but the ATF confirmed the targeted system was separate from its main network.
key_points: The ATF declared a 'major incident' following a cyberattack on a stand-alone system containing investigation targets' data.
The Qilin ransomware gang claimed responsibility but provided no evidence of the breach.
Qilin operates a ransomware-as-a-service model, leasing hacking tools to affiliates.
Federal law requires agencies to report 'major incidents' to Congress within a week of discovery.
The ATF system targeted was separate from its main network, mitigating broader impact.
Recent years have seen multiple U.S. government agencies declare major incidents due to cyberattacks.
